message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $103 and am on FREE_PARKING. I own the full orange monopoly but New York Avenue is mortgaged. I hold two of three pink properties. I own Marvin Gardens, which p4 needs to complete his yellow set.

p2 has $564 but weak holdings. p3 is in jail with $147 and mixed properties. p4 leads with $3101 and a dominant light blue monopoly.

I will keep Marvin Gardens and both pink properties to block p4 from completing his yellow set. I will not mortgage any orange properties or fund houses that would help p4 inherit them. With only $103 cash, I am deciding whether to end the turn, propose a trade, or mortgage a property.

I am weighing whether to mortgage a property. Pre-mortgaging costs 10% interest and loses rent, which is risky with only $103 cash. I am also checking upcoming rent from the next spaces, starting with Kentucky.

I mapped the upcoming spaces. Indiana, Illinois, and B&O are mortgaged so they pay no rent. Atlantic and Ventnor are p4's yellow monopoly with doubled rent at $44 and $52. I am checking whether p4 owns a green monopoly on Pennsylvania Avenue.

The upcoming rent is only about $18 to $52, so $103 covers it without needing to mortgage. I will not trade with p4 or sell Marvin and the pink properties to them. p2 offers little of value, and p3's dark blues are already blocked by my orange monopoly.

I checked whether p3 could complete a red monopoly, but Indiana and Illinois are mortgaged. I also noticed the game lists New York Avenue as unmortgageable, so I cannot use it to fund house building.

Unmortgaging New York Avenue costs $220, which exceeds my current cash. Building houses on the orange set is also impossible while it is mortgaged. I am now looking for a trade that could provide enough cash to unmortgage and build evenly without giving p4 a monopoly.

I am now considering trading Water Works for cash. A utility pair with p2 would not pressure p4, but the cash could fund unmortgaging and building on the orange set. The trade is unlikely to succeed because p2 has $564 and Water Works alone is weak.

I calculated that unmortgaging New York Avenue costs $220, leaving almost no cash for houses. Even with a full orange monopoly, the doubled rent is only about $30 per turn, which is too weak to threaten p4. Building three houses on each orange property requires roughly $900, so I would need to mortgage everything. The total mortgageable value of my holdings is about $535, bringing my combined cash to approximately $638.

Unmortgaging New York Avenue would leave only $418, enough for four houses but not the three each needed to threaten p4. Mortgaging Marvin and the pink properties would not give them to p4; they would simply be mortgaged. However, if I go bankrupt, mortgaged properties transfer to the creditor and must be paid back with 10% interest. That would let p4 inherit my mortgaged holdings and complete his monopolies.

I will not go bankrupt to p4. Even with hotels, p4's $3101 would survive a single hit. I am now looking for trades with p2 or p3 that could raise cash without completing p4's monopolies. p3's dark blues are worth about $175 to $250 each, but that is still too weak to bankrupt p4.

I will end the turn without trading or mortgaging. p3 is in jail with only $147, so he cannot build houses even if I gave him cash. I do not want to hand p2 or p3 money that could help them bankrupt me or let p4 inherit Boardwalk. p4 is in jail on turn two and will likely escape next turn.

I am now considering trading for North Carolina to block p4's green monopoly. p2 owns it mortgaged but has $564, so they may not sell it cheaply. I am also reviewing p4's full holdings: light blue hotels on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut; Virginia; Penn RR; Kentucky; Atlantic and Ventnor; Penn Ave; and Short Line.

I cannot afford North Carolina, which is mortgaged and worth more than I can pay. I am now considering proposing a trade to p3.
